opportunities.name: Mintek-SCi Grad Hackathon 2026
opportunities.location: Remote build; final hacking day + conference in person at Mintek, 200 Malibongwe Drive, Randburg

dates.final_hacking_day_hours: 08:00 report/build, 13:00 code submission deadline, 14:00 presentations (10 min/team)
dates.source: Mintek SCI Grad Hackathon selection letter, signed Boitumelo Lekalakala, dated 14 Aug 2026

prize.non_cash: Outstanding teams may be considered for vacation work at Mintek

opportunities.eligibility: University students, unemployed graduates, and interns under 35. Team-based, mentored.
opportunities.team_fit: Excellent — explicitly aimed at unemployed graduates. Directly on-target for your situation.
opportunities.what_to_build: Submitted abstract: REEFPRINT (Category: Problem 3 — Computer Vision for Real-Time Mineralogical Characterisation, by Lethabo). Rather than building a mineral classifier that competes with lab instruments (SEM/XRD/QEMSCAN), distills those instruments' existing output as a 'teacher' into a cheap optical model that reproduces their maps in seconds instead of days. Targets five Bushveld-relevant phases — chromite, orthopyroxene, plagioclase, base-metal sulphide, talc/serpentine — deliberately including base-metal sulphide even at <1% by area since that's where PGM economic value sits; the abstract commits to reporting per-class recall on that sub-1% class ahead of any aggregate accuracy number. Converts texture/liberation into three metallurgical response variables (liberation, reagent demand, grindability) feeding a plant setpoint recommendation with calibrated uncertainty — abstains rather than guessing when confidence is low. Frames cost/impact in Rand and tCO2e using real SA gazetted rates (Eskom Megaflex, carbon tax). Positioned as a module for Mintek's existing StarCS/FloatStar/MillStar platform, not a competing product. Code has since been re-scoped to match the submitted phase set.
deliverables: One-page abstract restating approach, methods/tech and expected outcomes — due 30 Aug 2026
Per-member info to Mintek: ID number, T-shirt size, contact details, mentor name/contact (or a request for one)
Completed solution submitted by 13:00 on the 1 Oct final hacking day
10-minute presentation to the judging panel, 1 Oct
Registration + attendance at the Mintek SCI Conference, 2 Oct — 5 finalist teams announced there, then originality/AI-generation/plagiarism authentication before the next stage
opportunities.notes: SELECTED — confirmed by Mintek's letter dated 14 Aug 2026 (signed Boitumelo Lekalakala). Team is in the hackathon, not just applied. Immediate action: one-page abstract due 30 Aug, plus per-member ID/T-shirt/contact/mentor info back to Mintek. Final hacking day is mandatory in-person at Mintek, 1 Oct (build until 13:00, present at 14:00, 10 min/team). Must also register for and attend the Mintek SCI Conference on 2 Oct, where the 5 finalists are announced and originality checks begin. Cash prizes now confirmed: R25k/R15k/R10k for top 3, plus possible vacation-work offers for standout teams.
